answer: Admission should bloom like a lotus, one stage per epoch: each stage demands a deed sealed inside a walnut-hard shell — the deed must embed the latest public-randomness beacon, so a farm cannot precompute it for a thousand clones in advance. Stages unfold strictly in sequence, so clones cost real time, not just keypairs. The final bloom requires a bridge: a co-signature from a peer in a different trust cluster, so a farm vouching only for its own clones can never cross.
